newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Banking sector pulls up the Moroccan bourse.
newsitem.headline: Banking sector pulls up the Moroccan bourse.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed higher on Tuesday due mainly to active trading in Moroccan banking shares, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 420.61, up 0.78 percent over Monday's session.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, continued its rise as expected, closing at 726 dirhams, up six dirhams on the previous session.
BCM, which is also the country's second largest bank due to its huge deposits "remains very attractive despite lack of paper," a market analyst said.

Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one the market blue chips, gained five dirhams to close at 407 dirhams. Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, closed at 310 dirhams, up 10 dirhams on the previous session.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private holding, pursued its upward trend to close at 427 dirhams, up 12 dirhams on Monday's session.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which holds stakes in more than 40 companies including the banking sector, remained stable at 575 dirhams.
Eight banks are listed on the Casablanca stock market.
"Generally speaking, the return of investors to the market after weeks of holidays was one of reasons behind the recent surge of the bourse stocks," a stockbroker at Maroc Inter Titres said.
Brasserie du Maroc, the country's main brewery, jumped 29 dirhams to close at 1,339 dirhams, traders said.
The bourse volume dropped to 23.9 million dirhams from 32.4 million dirhams from 138.1 million last week.
